Interface SseEmitter

public interface SseEmitter
Pushes server-sent events to one client: the text/event-stream response of an SSE route. The events are encoded like the events of a Publisher<Event> body: the data of an event is written as is if it is a CharSequence, and as JSON otherwise.

The end of the stream

The stream ends when the handler of the route returns: it is completed, or failed with the exception the handler threw. A handler that sends its events later, from callbacks or another thread, calls keepOpen() before it returns, and ends the stream with complete() or fail(Throwable). The stream also ends when the client disconnects. A send after the handler returned without keepOpen() fails, and the first one is logged as a warning.

The response

The response (200, text/event-stream, Cache-Control: no-cache, never compressed) is sent when the first event, comment or heartbeat is sent, or when the stream ends. Until then the stream can still be refused: an exception of the handler, or fail(Throwable), is answered by the error handling of the route, exactly like an exception of any other route, header(CharSequence, CharSequence) adds headers to the response, and respond(HttpResponse) answers with another response instead of the event stream. After that, a failure ends the response abruptly: it is logged, and the connection is closed. To send the response before the first event, send a comment or configure a heartbeat. Until the response is sent, a disconnect of the client is noticed only by the next send: a stream that waits for its first event should send a comment or a heartbeat first.

Backpressure

The stream counts the bytes the connection has not taken yet: bytes of events that are queued because the client reads slower than the events are sent. The stage returned by send(Event) completes once the bytes of the event, together with the bytes queued before it, are below the high-water mark: immediately if the client keeps up, otherwise once the connection took enough of the queue. Waiting for the stage before the next send paces the sender to the client: a handler that sends from a loop continues in the stage, or, on a virtual thread or a thread of a blocking executor, waits for it, e.g. with send(event).toCompletableFuture().join(). isWritable() tells whether a send would complete immediately, for senders that would rather drop events than wait, such as a broadcast to many clients.

The queue is bounded: a send while sixteen times the high-water mark are already queued fails with a StreamOverflowException, and ends the stream, since the client would otherwise miss events. A sender that awaits its sends never reaches the bound. A sender that does not, e.g. one that calls send(Event) for every message of a source that does not wait, fails a client that reads slower than it sends once 1 MiB is queued with the default high-water mark of 64 KiB: such a sender checks isWritable() and drops or coalesces events, or raises the bound with highWaterMark(int) (or micronaut.server.responses.stream.high-water-mark) if its bursts are bounded.

Threads

All methods can be called from any thread. The events are written in the order their sends were called. The stages complete, and the onClose(Consumer) callbacks run, on a thread chosen by the server, usually the event loop of the connection, with the propagated context of the route handler: a continuation must not block. When the client disconnects, the pending and the later sends fail with a ConnectionClosedException, and the onClose(Consumer) callbacks run with that exception.

  • Method Details

    • send

      CompletionStage<Void> send(Event<?> event)
      Send an event. The send does not wait: wait for the returned stage before the next send to pace the sender to the client. Sends that do not wait queue the events of a slow client until the queue overflows and the stream fails, see the class documentation.
      Parameters:
      event - The event
      Returns:
      Completes when the event was queued below the high-water mark (see the class documentation), or exceptionally if the stream is closed, the client disconnected, the queue overflowed, or the event could not be encoded (the stream stays open)

    • send

      Parameters:

      Returns:
      Completes like send(Event)

    • header

      SseEmitter header(CharSequence name, CharSequence value)
      Add a header to the response, before it is sent: before the first event, comment or heartbeat, e.g. X-Accel-Buffering: no for a proxy that would buffer the stream. The status and the Content-Type of the response cannot be changed: to answer with another status, throw an exception or fail the stream.
      Parameters:
      name - The name of the header
      value - The value
      Returns:
      This emitter
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if the response was already sent
      IllegalArgumentException - if the header is Content-Type

    • respond

      void respond(HttpResponse<?> response)
      Answer with another response instead of the event stream, before the first event, comment or heartbeat: e.g. a single JSON message, or 202 Accepted without a body, for a protocol in which the server decides per request whether to stream, such as the MCP Streamable HTTP transport. The headers added with header(CharSequence, CharSequence) are added to the response, unless it has them, and a body without a content type is written as JSON. The stream ends: the onClose(Consumer) callbacks run with null.
      Parameters:
      response - The response
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if the response was already sent, or the stream ended

    • keepOpen

      SseEmitter keepOpen()
      Keep the stream open after the handler returns: the handler sends the events later, from callbacks or another thread, and ends the stream with complete() or fail(Throwable). Without it, the stream ends when the handler returns.
      Returns:
      This emitter
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if the handler already returned

    • heartbeat

      SseEmitter heartbeat(Duration period)
      Send a comment line when no event was sent for the given period, to keep the connection and the proxies on the way from timing it out as idle. The first heartbeat sends the response if no event was sent yet: an error or another response after it can no longer be answered. Heartbeats are skipped while the stream is not writable. The default is micronaut.server.responses.stream.sse-heartbeat, none if not set, which starts once the response is sent, so that it never sends the response itself.
      Parameters:
      period - The period, Duration.ZERO to stop the heartbeat
      Returns:
      This emitter

    • highWaterMark

      Parameters:
      bytes - The high-water mark, positive
      Returns:
      This emitter

    • onClose

      SseEmitter onClose(Consumer<@Nullable Throwable> callback)
      Run a callback when the stream closes: with null when it was completed (or when the response of a HEAD request, which has no body, was sent), and with the cause when it failed, overflowed, or the client disconnected. A callback added after the stream closed runs at once.
      Parameters:
      callback - The callback
      Returns:
      This emitter

    • complete

      void complete()
      End the stream: the queued events are still written, then the response ends. Pending send stages complete. Does nothing if the stream is already closed.

    • fail

      void fail(Throwable cause)
      Fail the stream. Before the response was sent, the failure is answered by the error handling of the route; after, the response ends abruptly and the failure is logged. Pending send stages fail with the cause. Does nothing if the stream is already closed.
      Parameters:
      cause - The failure
